England.difference_en: England formally develops perimeter from Year 3 and extends it to more complex shapes in later years. China's second learning stage includes perimeter and area, while exact current PEP semester placement still requires verification.
England.why_en: Perimeter measures boundary length, whereas area measures the size of the interior surface.
England.classroom_use_en: Use string to trace perimeter and unit squares to cover area on the same shape, then compare the units.

US.difference_en: Common Core Grade 3 develops perimeter and area together and explicitly includes problems with the same perimeter but different areas, or the same area but different perimeters.
US.why_en: Direct comparison helps pupils separate the two attributes rather than treating their formulae as interchangeable.
US.classroom_use_en: Draw two rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas and explain what changed.

England.difference_en: England Year 4 establishes area by counting squares; Year 5 calculates rectangle area and estimates irregular areas.
England.why_en: The area formula is more meaningful when it grows from rows and columns of equal square units rather than being introduced as a rule first.
England.classroom_use_en: Cover a rectangle with unit squares and connect rows × columns with the total number of squares.

US.difference_en: Common Core Grade 3 formally defines area using unit squares and connects rectangle area with multiplication and addition.
US.why_en: Area and rectangular arrays share the same multiplicative structure.
US.classroom_use_en: Interpret a 4×6 array both as 24 objects and as an area of 24 square units.

England.difference_en: England Years 5-6 extend from rectangle area to parallelogram and triangle formulae. China's third learning stage includes the areas of several plane figures.
England.why_en: Deriving a formula through cutting, rearranging or relating to a known figure gives meaning to the quantities in the formula.
England.classroom_use_en: Before using the triangle-area formula, combine two congruent triangles into a parallelogram.

US.difference_en: Common Core Grade 6 finds areas of triangles, special quadrilaterals and polygons through composition and decomposition.
US.why_en: New formulae are connected to known area relationships instead of treated as unrelated rules.
US.classroom_use_en: For each new formula, include one task showing how it can be derived from a known shape.

England.difference_en: England Year 5 begins estimating volume and capacity; Year 6 calculates cuboid volume in cubic units. China's third learning stage develops volume, capacity and related units.
England.why_en: Volume is three-dimensional space and is built from layers of unit cubes.
England.classroom_use_en: Count the unit cubes in one layer first, then multiply by the number of layers.

US.difference_en: Common Core Grade 5 formally defines volume using unit cubes and connects volume with multiplication and addition.
US.why_en: Unit cubes give length × width × height a concrete quantity meaning.
US.classroom_use_en: Before using a formula, ask how many cubes are in one layer and how many layers there are.

England.difference_en: England Year 6 uses the cuboid-volume formula and connects it with cubic units and linear dimensions.
England.why_en: The formula compresses the structure of rows × columns × layers of unit cubes.
England.classroom_use_en: Ask why a 4 cm by 3 cm by 2 cm cuboid has a volume in cm³ rather than cm².

US.difference_en: Common Core Grade 5 uses V=l×w×h and V=b×h for rectangular prisms; Grade 6 extends volume work to fractional edge lengths.
US.why_en: The formula remains connected to unit-cube structure and multiplication.
US.classroom_use_en: For a 4×3×2 prism, sketch the layers before writing the formula.
